credentials.name: anthropic
credentials.scope: Claude API direct access for OpenClaw agents, the felix-doc-auditor scripts-first driver, and the felix-heartbeat-gate (#490)
credentials.storage: /home/claude/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite (OpenClaw 2026.6+ per-agent SQLite auth store, openclaw-gateway; sub-agents inherit via read-through), /data/services/openclaw/secrets/anthropic (file, 0600 — primary source for the felix-doc-auditor driver and felix-heartbeat-gate; also the openclaw-gateway backup)
credentials.notes: Three consumers post-#490, sharing the same key value. (1) openclaw-gateway: holds the key via OpenClaw's per-agent SQLite auth store (openclaw-agent.sqlite, 2026.6+) on the 'main' agent and proxies API calls for all openclaw-launched agents (felix-admin-capture, -habits, -tasker, -escalation, -calendar). Sub-agents inherit auth from main via read-through and need no separate update on rotation. Pre-2026.6 used file-backed auth-profiles.json; the upgrade migration ran by `openclaw doctor --fix` moved every agent's profile into SQLite — see docs/runbooks/openclaw-ops.md § Upgrade procedure for the post-upgrade gate. (2) felix-doc-auditor-driver: reads the key directly from /data/services/openclaw/secrets/anthropic (0600, claude:claude) at the start of each hourly systemd tick and calls api.anthropic.com via the anthropic-python SDK. The driver does not route through openclaw-gateway. (3) felix-heartbeat-gate (#490): same file-read pattern as the doc-auditor driver — reads the key at the start of each 30-minute tick and calls api.anthropic.com directly via the anthropic-python SDK with claude-haiku-4-5. The gate does not route through openclaw-gateway. On rotation, all three copies must be updated in lock-step (openclaw's native store + the file consumed by both Python drivers). Behavior on a missing/invalid key: tick fails fast with a structured error in the respective last-tick.json / last-gate-decision.json; the gate additionally invokes its fallback path (ESCALATE_TO_SONNET) so observation is never silently dropped. Key contents are never logged by either driver.
credentials.expiry_notes: Anthropic API keys do not have a fixed expiry date. Created 2026-06-12. Can be rotated manually via console.anthropic.com. Recommend review annually or if a security incident occurs. Rotation impact post-#490: all three consumers (openclaw-gateway, felix-doc-auditor-driver, felix-heartbeat-gate) must pick up the new key — restart openclaw-gateway + the next felix-doc-auditor tick verifies via last-tick.json + the next felix-heartbeat-gate tick verifies via last-gate-decision.json.

Felix-bot token was assigned a 3-year expiry (2026-05-17 → 2029-05-17) at operator discretion; any future date is supported by the UI. Plan a rotation before 2029-05-17 to maintain Felix operations continuity. Cron alert via credential-health-check.service should fire 30 days before expiry (~2029-04-17).

credentials.name: google-workspace-client
credentials.scope: OAuth 2.0 Desktop client_secret for Google Workspace via gog (covers Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Contacts, Sheets, Docs)
credentials.notes: OAuth Desktop client_secret downloaded from Google Cloud Console (project felix-openclaw-gog). Ingested into gog via `gog auth credentials`. Does not expire on its own — rotated only if compromise is suspected. Used during `gog auth add` runs; routine API calls do not re-read this file.

credentials.name: gog-keyring-password
credentials.scope: gog keyring encryption passphrase (file backend) — protects the refresh token in /home/claude/.config/gogcli/credentials.json
used_by: gog (via GOG_KEYRING_PASSWORD env var, exported in claude's ~/.bashrc for interactive sessions and via the openclaw-gateway-env file for the OpenClaw gateway and its child agent sessions — see openclaw-gateway-env entry below and runbook Pitfall 4)
credentials.notes: 32-byte base64 random passphrase generated via `openssl rand -base64 32`. Exported into the claude shell via `GOG_KEYRING_PASSWORD="$(cat /data/services/openclaw/secrets/gog-keyring-password)"` in claude's ~/.bashrc. Required because office2 is headless and gog's default D-Bus SecretService backend is unavailable (see runbook Pitfall 2).
credentials.expiry_notes: Static passphrase. Rotating it requires re-running the full gog OAuth flow because it encrypts the refresh-token bucket. Rotate annually or on suspected compromise.

credentials.name: gog-credentials-keyring
credentials.scope: gog-managed encrypted credentials + refresh-token bucket (encrypted with gog-keyring-password)
credentials.notes: Encrypted bucket managed by gog itself. Contents are not read or written directly by operators or agents — only via `gog auth *` commands. Encrypted with the passphrase from `gog-keyring-password`. Rebuilt by re-running the OAuth flow if the passphrase rotates or the file is lost.
credentials.expiry_notes: Holds OAuth refresh tokens. Refresh tokens have no fixed expiry but are revoked by: password change on the linked Google account, 6+ months inactivity, Google security review, or manual revocation at myaccount.google.com/permissions. Re-mint via `gog auth add <email> --services ... --remote` per the runbook.

credentials.name: openclaw-gateway-env
credentials.scope: Systemd EnvironmentFile that injects GOG_KEYRING_BACKEND + GOG_KEYRING_PASSWORD into the openclaw-gateway service and all child agent sessions. Without this, the gateway's child processes cannot decrypt gog-credentials-keyring and `gog auth list` / live API calls fail from inside agent sessions.
used_by: openclaw-gateway.service (systemd-user unit) via EnvironmentFile= directive in the drop-in at ~/.config/systemd/user/openclaw-gateway.service.d/env.conf
credentials.notes: Plain KEY=VALUE env-file format consumed by systemd's EnvironmentFile directive. Contains GOG_KEYRING_BACKEND=file and a duplicate of gog-keyring-password's contents as GOG_KEYRING_PASSWORD=<value>. Required because systemd-launched services do not source ~/.bashrc, so the interactive-shell exports for GOG_* env vars don't reach the gateway or its child agent sessions. See runbook Pitfall 4 for full context. If the underlying gog-keyring-password rotates, regenerate this file with the new value: `PW=$(cat /data/services/openclaw/secrets/gog-keyring-password); printf 'GOG_KEYRING_BACKEND=file\nGOG_KEYRING_PASSWORD=%s\n' "$PW" > /data/services/openclaw/secrets/openclaw-gateway.env && chmod 600 /data/services/openclaw/secrets/openclaw-gateway.env && systemctl --user restart openclaw-gateway`.
credentials.expiry_notes: Derived from gog-keyring-password — regenerate whenever that rotates. No independent expiry.

credentials.name: kg-felix-bot-pat
credentials.scope: GitHub classic PAT for kg-felix-bot service-account identity. Used by Felix agents (felix-doc-auditor, felix-core-digest-signals) for git push and gh CLI actions, providing a separate audit-trail identity from kentonium3.
used_by: future Felix agents operating as kg-felix-bot
credentials.updated_by: #490 + 2026-06-03 rotation (1-year expiry adopted after sub-agent leak incident)
credentials.notes: Classic PAT with scopes: repo, read:org, workflow. Bot account at github.com/kg-felix-bot has 2FA enabled; email alias kentgale+felix-bot@gmail.com routes to kentgale@gmail.com. Required classic (not fine-grained) because fine-grained PATs limit access to resources the bot owns; bot is a collaborator on kentonium3/kg-automation, not an owner. Post-#490 the deterministic signal filer in felix-core-digest (tick.py → felix-file-issue.py) also operates under this identity — no new credential, same `gh auth status` shows kg-felix-bot active.
credentials.expiry_notes: Rotated 2026-06-03 with an explicit 1-year expiry (was previously created 2026-05-11 with no expiry). Operator policy shifted to bounded-lifetime PATs after a sub-agent on a research mission leaked the prior token into a session record (2026-06 incident). Old token was revoked at the same time. Rotation procedure: generate new PAT in github.com settings for kg-felix-bot account with a 1-year expiry, then on office2: `gh auth logout` && `gh auth login --hostname github.com --git-protocol https` with the new token. Verify with `gh auth status` showing kg-felix-bot active. Post-#490: rotation also affects felix-core-digest-signals (deterministic filer in tick.py) — same gh CLI identity, no separate action required. The credential-health-check.service will fire 30 days before expires_at (~2027-05-05) via the Vikunja escalation path.

credentials.name: kentonium3-gh-oauth
credentials.scope: GitHub auth credential for Kent's personal kentonium3 identity. Used for manual git operations and gh CLI from Mac. Distinct from kg-felix-bot-pat which is the agent identity on office2.
credentials.storage: macOS Keychain (managed by gh CLI; profile recorded in ~/.config/gh/hosts.yml)
used_by: Kent (manual git + gh CLI from Mac)
credentials.notes: OAuth user-to-server token issued by GitHub CLI's OAuth app (token prefix gho_). Scopes as of 2026-05-11: gist, project, read:org, repo, workflow. This is NOT a manually-created classic or fine-grained PAT — rotation is via `gh auth login --hostname github.com`, not via the 'Generate new PAT' flow in GitHub settings. office2 does not hold a copy of this credential; kgale and claude users on office2 use the kg-felix-bot identity instead.
credentials.expiry_notes: OAuth user-to-server tokens issued by gh CLI do not carry a fixed expiry but can be revoked by: rotating via `gh auth logout --hostname github.com && gh auth login --hostname github.com --git-protocol https`; revoking GitHub CLI's OAuth app at https://github.com/settings/applications; account password change; or extended inactivity. macOS Keychain stores the new token automatically after re-auth. Cross-check scopes match expectations after each rotation: `gh auth status` should show `repo`, `read:org`, `workflow` at minimum.
credentials.created_date_note: Predates manifest tracking; Kent's gh auth on Mac has been active for an extended period without manual rotation memory.

credentials.name: kg-felix-bot-project-sync-pat
credentials.scope: GitHub classic PAT for kg-felix-bot, scope=project only. Used by the priority-field-sync job in .github/workflows/spec-lifecycle.yml to mirror issue priority labels (P1-* / P2-* / P3-*) onto the Felix Roadmap project's Priority single-select field.
credentials.storage: GitHub Actions secret PROJECT_SYNC_PAT on kentonium3/kg-automation
credentials.notes: Separate from kg-felix-bot-pat (which carries repo, read:org, workflow scopes). Created with project scope only to honor the credential-hygiene principle that triggered the 2026-06-03 kg-felix-bot-pat rotation — narrower blast radius if leaked. Requires kg-felix-bot to be a collaborator on the Felix Roadmap user-owned project (added 2026-06-04). The token is not stored on office2 or anywhere outside GitHub Actions secret storage.
credentials.expiry_notes: Issued 2026-06-04 with a 1-year expiry to match the cadence of kg-felix-bot-pat. Rotation procedure: generate new PAT under github.com/kg-felix-bot (scope=project, 1-year expiry), update the PROJECT_SYNC_PAT repo secret, then revoke the old token. The credential-health-check.service will fire ~30 days before expires_at (~2027-05-04) via the Vikunja escalation path.

credentials.name: felix-deployer-ntfy-topic
credentials.scope: Private ntfy.sh topic identifier consumed by scripts/deploy/felix-deployer/notify.py for failure-notification dispatch. Exported as FELIX_DEPLOYER_NTFY_TOPIC into the felix-deployer.service process environment via systemd EnvironmentFile= on office2.
credentials.notes: Publish-only secret: knowing the topic value enables passive listening to failure notifications but cannot be used to impersonate the felix-deployer service, mint deploys, or modify state. Operator subscribes the ntfy phone app to the same topic. Provisioned out-of-band on office2 (env-file is never committed). The systemd unit uses EnvironmentFile=- (leading dash) so the unit starts cleanly if the file is missing — notify.py then returns LibResult(ok=False, error_code=NTFY_MISSING_TOPIC) and the operator discovers failures by polling deploys/failed/.
credentials.expiry_notes: No automatic expiry. Rotate only on suspected leak (the topic appears in a non-private log, screenshot, or shared context). Rotation procedure: ssh office2-claude, edit /home/claude/.config/felix-deployer/env to new randomly-generated topic, restart felix-deployer.timer (or wait for next tick), subscribe ntfy phone app to the new topic, unsubscribe from the old one.

credentials.name: felix-alert-ntfy-topic
credentials.scope: Private ntfy.sh topic identifier for the unified felix-alert bus (scripts/common/alert_bus/). Exported as FELIX_ALERT_NTFY_TOPIC into every emitting runtime — via systemd EnvironmentFile= on felix-deployer.service, felix-health-check.service, and agent-prompt-sync.service, and by scripts/common/alert_bus.sh sourcing the file directly for the cron-launched security-monitor audit (which inherits no systemd EnvironmentFile).
credentials.notes: Publish-only secret: knowing the topic value lets a passive listener read alert bodies (which carry error text and paths) but cannot impersonate any emitter, mint deploys, or modify state. A NEW dedicated high-entropy topic (D5) — do NOT reuse felix-deployer-ntfy-topic. Operator subscribes the ntfy phone app to the same topic. Provisioned out-of-band on office2 (env-file is never committed — the C-002 exception; only the placeholder template is committed). Each systemd unit uses EnvironmentFile=- (leading dash) so it starts cleanly if the file is missing; the bus then returns AlertResult(ok=False) with NTFY_MISSING_TOPIC and the deploy preflight (scripts/deploy/deploy-unified-alert-bus.py --dry-run) reports the absent file.
credentials.expiry_notes: No automatic expiry. Rotate only on suspected leak (the topic appears in a non-private log, screenshot, or shared context). Rotation procedure: ssh office2-claude, edit /home/claude/.config/felix/alert-bus/env to a new randomly-generated topic, restart the emitting timers (or wait for the next tick), subscribe the ntfy phone app to the new topic, unsubscribe from the old one.

credentials.name: felix-google-personal-calendar
credentials.scope: Personal Google Calendar event CRUD (calendar.events) + Sheets read/write (spreadsheets) for Kent's personal account kentgale@gmail.com, consumed directly by the Felix calendar helper and the Felix time-log Sheets helper — NOT via gog
credentials.storage: ~/.config/felix/google/personal/client_secret.json + token.json (per-account store; file 0600, dir 0700). On office2: /home/claude/.config/felix/google/personal/. FELIX_GOOGLE_DIR overrides the base dir for test isolation.
used_by: felix-admin-calendar (judgment layer — invokes the calendar helper, holds no gog calendar skill)
scripts/google/timelog.py (time-log normalizer — invokes the Sheets helper, #703)
main (invokes timelog via exec for the WhatsApp time-logging recognizer, #703)
credentials.notes: Authorized-user OAuth2 credential (client_secret.json = Desktop OAuth client from GCP project felix-personal, External + 'In production'; token.json = authorized-user token incl. refresh_token). First concrete delivery of accepted RFC #681: Felix owns the Google Calendar surface directly via google-api-python-client instead of shelling to gog. Separate and independent from the gog credential family (google-workspace-client / gog-keyring-password / gog-credentials-keyring), which remain active for gog's other surfaces (Gmail/Drive/Contacts/Sheets/Docs) — gog is NOT retired by this mission. Token minted once interactively on the Mac with the FINAL scope, then durable per RFC #681 (personal @gmail account + 'In production' app yields a non-expiring authorization; the #572 7-day Testing-mode expiry does NOT apply here). office2 NEVER runs interactive consent: on any auth failure the helper exits 3 (calendar) / 1 (sheets, mapped from SheetsAuthError) with an actionable 're-mint on the Mac' message and performs no mutation (fail-safe, FR-006/C-002). Multi-account-ready: adding the intentional.biz account is create its own directory + drop credentials + pass its account name — no helper code change (FR-005). Access tokens are obtained at runtime and refreshed in place; never committed (NFR-004). Staged Mac-side then copied to office2 same path (manual operator step; the deploy manifest only verifies presence). #703 (felix-time-logging) re-mints this token ONCE with the combined `calendar + spreadsheets` scopes (one operator re-consent, Kent-in-the-loop) so the same per-account credential now backs both the calendar helper and the new Sheets time-log helper — both loaders are scope-agnostic at load/refresh time (never force a scope), so the combined-scope token does not break the calendar helper. See docs/runbooks/timelog.md for the re-consent procedure.
credentials.expiry_notes: OAuth2 refresh tokens have no fixed expiry but are revoked on: Google account password change, 6+ months inactivity, Google security review, or manual revocation at myaccount.google.com/permissions. Because the app is 'In production' (not Testing), the 7-day Testing-mode refresh-token expiry does NOT apply. (#572; the gog OAuth app is now published as well, so the 7-day Testing-mode expiry no longer applies to the gog credential either — see #731.) Re-mint procedure on scope/auth failure: run the interactive consent flow on the Mac with the combined calendar.events + spreadsheets scopes, then re-stage token.json to office2 (0600), and verify BOTH `calendar_helper --self-check` and `sheets_helper --self-check` return ok. See docs/runbooks/calendar-helper-ops.md and docs/runbooks/timelog.md.
credentials.updated_by: felix-time-logging-01KX79HT (#703 — adds the spreadsheets scope for the time-log Sheets helper; one-time combined re-consent)

credentials.name: vikunja-api-kent
credentials.scope: Full Vikunja system access as the kent user — Felix configuration/system changes (labels, saved filters, projects) and applying labels to tasks, which Vikunja's per-user-scoped model requires the owning (kent) user to perform
credentials.notes: Owned by the kent Vikunja user (all-permissions API token). Added by #715 because Vikunja scopes labels/filters per user: taxonomy labels created by felix-bot are invisible in kent's UI, so config objects kent must see/manage have to be created as kent. Deliberately reintroduces a kent-scoped token that #304 rotated to felix-bot — the felix-bot/kent audit separation is retained for task WRITES (vikunja-api) but knowingly given up for config changes (they attribute to kent). Verified 2026-07-12: felix-bot CAN read/filter kent-owned labels on shared tasks but CANNOT attach them (403), so label-attach uses this kent token. See identity-model.md §Agent Service Accounts.
credentials.expiry_notes: Vikunja UI requires an explicit expiry; operator set 2027-07-12 (1-year, created 2026-07-12 10:58:07). credential-health-check.service should alert ~30 days before (~2027-06-12). Rotate before expiry to maintain Felix's Vikunja config capability.

rules: No credentials in committed files — ever
Interactive auth for manual scripts (setup_vikunja.py pattern)
Stored tokens for agent/automated use in office2 scoped secrets store
Credential names are stable identifiers used across documentation and code
